newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss freeze Mobutu's villa but not other assets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss freeze Mobutu's villa but not other assets.

text.p: Switzerland ordered a freeze on Friday on the multi-million-dollar villa of Mobutu Sese Seko as the Zairean leader teetered on the verge of being deposed.

A government statement said federal police and justice authorities asked the canton of Vaud to put the sprawling luxury villa near Lausanne on the real estate register as "blocked" and "cannot be transferred until further notice".

The 66-year-old veteran Zairean strongman, sick with cancer and facing rebel forces within striking distance of his capital, left Kinshasa on Friday for his northern jungle palace at Gbadolite. His departure triggered intense speculation he may be on his way into exile abroad.

This is the first time Switzerland has ordered a freeze on the property of a ruler still in power. It stopped short, however, of ordering a freeze on other Mobutu assets estimated by Swiss media to total $4 billion.

The government said a request to do so by a Zairean prosecutor did not contain sufficient detail on other alleged assets of Mobutu and "for the moment, does not allow the possible adoption of other measures".
Switzerland would be asking for further information on this issue, the statement said.
The moves were in response to a request from the public prosecutor of the rebel-held Zairean city of Lubumbashi to freeze all assets Mobutu may have in the Alpine country.
The government said the prosecutor, appointed by Mobutu although he later switched allegiance to the rebels, "appears therefore to be a competent representative of the Zairean judicial authorities".
The Swiss decision in no way equated to recognition of a government led by rebel chief Laurent Kabila, it said.

The unprecedented Swiss move may increase pressure on other countries where Mobutu has assets or property to follow suit. Rebel representatives in Switzerland on Thursday asked the United States, France, Belgium and countries including Austria and Portugal to freeze any Mobutu assets they may have.

Mobutu has a string of luxury properties including an apartment in Paris, property in Brussels, a south of France holiday home and an estate in the Portuguese Algarve which also houses his vintage wine cellar reputedly with 14,000 bottles.
His Spanish interests reportedly include a luxury villa and hotel in Marbella and a home in Madrid.
Mobutu's villa in Savigny near Lausanne, kept spotless and hidden from prying eyes, has a market value of some $5.5 million, according to Swiss media.

Photographs from the air of the luxury estate, which Mobutu bought for his first wife Marie-Antoinette in 1968, show a huge house, swimming pool, garages, a pond surrounded by trees and a small chalet in the sprawling garden.

Mobutu's bank accounts are less visible. Switzerland's top banking watchdog, the Federal Banking Commission, has ordered an official search for Mobutu accounts among banks and given them until the end of May to report.

If the search finds any sizeable accounts belonging to Mobutu, some fear Swiss banks may get caught up in a legal wrangle similar to that surrounding the millions of former Philippines ruler Ferdinand Marcos, now the subject of a long court battle.
